review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp-related pieces against the library definitions. The file has no simp attributes of its own. Its only simp-interface issues are the two small bridge lemmas about `unipotent`, `unipotentGL2` and `iotaGL`. I read `unipotentGL2` and its simp lemma `unipotentGL2_coe`, and `iotaGL`, `coe_iotaGL` and `iotaGL_unipotentGL2`. I also grepped the repository for other copies of the `unipotent`/`unipotentGL2` bridge lemma. I did not run Lean, so the suggested replacements are untested. I did not check whether adding `@[simp]` to a lemma in an upstream definitions file would interact badly with other simp sets in files I did not open. The rest of the file (the Whittaker span induction, the determinant lemmas and the main proof) uses `simp` as ordinary closing or normalising calls, and I found nothing there that fits this rubric.

findings.excerpt: theorem unipotentGL2_eq_unipotent (x : F) : (unipotentGL2 x : GL (Fin 2) F) = unipotent x := by
findings.problem: The canonical bridge between `UnramifiedWhittaker.unipotent` and `AutomorphicForm.unipotentGL2` is missing from the definitions files and is not a simp lemma. At least four other solution files re-prove it as a local theorem named `unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2`, all oriented `unipotent x = unipotentGL2 x`. This file adds a fifth copy, with the opposite orientation, `unipotentGL2 x = unipotent x`. Neither orientation is registered with `simp`, so `simp` cannot identify the two spellings of the same unipotent element. Users have to pick a direction by hand with `rw [← …]` or `rw […]`, as at lines 52 and 213. Two competing orientations in the library would also make it unsafe to tag either one `@[simp]` later.
findings.proposed_change: Put one canonical lemma `unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2 (x : K) : UnramifiedWhittaker.unipotent x = AutomorphicForm.unipotentGL2 x` next to the definitions. Tag it `@[simp]`, because `unipotentGL2` already has the simp lemmas `unipotentGL2_coe`, `unipotentGL2_zero` and the additive structure. Delete this file's reversed copy and use the canonical lemma instead. Line 213 then becomes `rw [hgk, mul_one, ← unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2]`, or `simp` can do it.
findings.benefit: There is one normal form (`unipotentGL2`) and one orientation across the library. Goals mixing the two spellings can be closed by `simp` without hand-picked `rw` directions. The five duplicate local copies can be removed.

evidence.excerpt: theorem unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2 {K : Type*} [Field K] (x : K) : unipotent x = unipotentGL2 x

findings.excerpt: theorem iotaGL_unipotent (x : F) : iotaGL (unipotent x) = upperUnipotent3 x 0 0 := by
findings.problem: The library already has `iotaGL_unipotentGL2`, which gives `iotaGL (unipotentGL2 x) = upperUnipotent3 x 0 0`. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Because `unipotent` and `unipotentGL2` are not linked by a simp lemma, `iotaGL (unipotent x)` stays unnormalised. This file therefore re-proves the statement from scratch, with `fin_cases` and `simp [embedMat2, …]`. It is used by `rw` at line 202. A manual duplicate proof is the symptom of the missing simp rule.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `iotaGL_unipotentGL2` as `@[simp]` in `Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_Carrier`. With the canonical `@[simp] unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2` from the previous finding, `simp` then rewrites `iotaGL (unipotent x)` to `upperUnipotent3 x 0 0` directly. This local lemma can then be deleted. The step at line 202 becomes `simp only [map_mul, unipotent_eq_unipotentGL2, iotaGL_unipotentGL2, …]`, or `simp`. If the lemma is kept, its proof should be `by rw [← unipotentGL2_eq_unipotent]; exact iotaGL_unipotentGL2 x`.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated `fin_cases` proof. It also gives `iotaGL` applied to a unipotent matrix a single simp-normal form, `upperUnipotent3 x 0 0`, whichever of the two unipotent constructors was written.
